item.title: Ask HN: What is the future of software manager job? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
I am seeing the term "player-coach" thrown by CEOs and VCs. I think this originated somewhere in VC circle and "move fast" philisophy.

While there is a lot of waste and many managers are doing coordination only rather than adding value, it is hard to imagine having a manager 20+ reports and then doing coding on top of that.

I am looking for EM job and barely seeing any responses. I have remained fairly hands-on but I don't write production code every single day. I have one FAANG, a few mid size companies (equivalent of PayPal), and two startups on resume. How are you all doing and what are you doing to get responses for manager roles?

item.title: Seeking small angel/co-founder for 7-year solo deterministic AI runtime project (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
After 7+ years of solo, self-funded research, I built a deterministic Linguistic Runtime - a fundamental solution to the modeling problem in AI.It is about creating and manipulating reality models directly from natural language without LLM.

Grok (the least sycophantic AI) audit scores:

• Logical Soundness and Consistency: 9.7/10 • Demonstration: 9.3/10 • Roadmap: 9.3/10

Demo (proof of the modeling solution):

Sign-in → Inventory item addition → Order creation → Total/tax calculation with dynamic rules. All via pure natural language. No LLMs. No coding/code generation. No predefined classes/schemas/templates. No back-end or front-end APIs. Natural language is the API.

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Y1I04_T5-RWTQzS1HngCzW5vIaeS7q4W/view?usp=drive_link

Sovereign Shell (Phase 1) is the first commercial product: a practical utility that turns natural language intent into reliable system commands for sysadmins and DevOps engineers. It is the most capital-efficient first step and will create a hardened codebase and industrial proof for future phases.

Roadmap (single codebase): Phase 1: Sovereign Shell (current focus) Phase 2: Software Builder - AI acts directly as software with dynamic UI Phase 3: Domain-specific chatbots with real understanding and psychology Phase 4: Hardware/edge integration I am now looking for a small angel investment or co-founder help to incorporate the company and ship Phase 1 in the coming months.

Full Grok audit report: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IDIyh5MMQTXa5ccWNmbRiGXone_8-dC1/view?usp=sharing

Demo + thesis: https://theantagonistai.substack.com/

I can share a detailed pitch deck with serious interested parties.Any genuine interest, advice, feedback,introductions orguidance would be greatly appreciated.

item.title: Show HN: Git for AI Agents (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
hi guys. been working on something i think is fundamentally missing in today's workflow with ai agents.

vcs.

i find myself struggling with questions that agents can't answer like "why did you do it?", "when did u delete this folder? why?", etc. or trying to /rewind (after a /compact...) or basically `bisect` to find when and why something was done by the agent in the current / previous session.

just like git did for code, i think we are the same core capabilities with ai agents

so...

i developed an open source solution for that (currently supporting claude code)

would love to get feedback, contribution or maybe other ideas or solutions you find for those problems.

item.title: Ask HN: We just had an actual UUID v4 collision... (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
I know what you're thinking... and I still can't believe it, but...

This morning, our database flagged a duplicate UUID (v4). I checked, thinking it may have been a double-insert bug or something, but no.

The original UUID was from a record added in 2025 (about a year ago), and today the system inserted a new document with a fresh UUIDv4 and it came up with the exact same one:

b6133fd6-70fe-4fe3-bed6-8ca8fc9386cd

We're using this: https://www.npmjs.com/package/uuid

I thought this is technically impossible, and it will never happen, and since we're not modifying the UUIDs in any way, I really wonder how that.... is possible!? We're literally only calling:

import { v4 as uuidv4 } from "uuid";

const document_id = uuidv4();

... and then insert into the database, that's it.

Additionally, the database only has about 15.000 records, and now one collision. Statistically... impossible.

Has that ever happened to anyone?! What in the...
